text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of nearly 14%. The drop reflects deteriorating refining economics: US oil prices dropped from the mid-$80s to $82.24 per barrel while global crude sits higher at $91.80, narrowing the profit margin refiners earn on each barrel processed. With refineries already running at 97.5% capacity and gasoline and diesel inventories remaining elevated, there's limited room for refiners to pass costs along or boost throughput to offset thinner margins.

The timing aligns with mounting geopolitical tensions in oil-producing regions — attacks on Saudi infrastructure, sanctions tightening around Iran, and ongoing Ukraine-Russia conflict — that have kept crude prices volatile rather than trending higher. For a refiner, that instability combined with flat-to-weak refining spreads creates a difficult near-term backdrop, even as the company remains heavily utilized.
